This review is coming from a well experienced Minesweeper player: This game is painfully easy and very uninteresting. The rougelike mechanics are boring, poorly explained, surface-level and uninteractive. Very poor variety that gives little extra replay-ability or intrigue when compared to normal Minesweeper. Boss fights are boring and change nothing about the board other than giving the player a timer, of which is based off of your score in the previous boards. This means that if you are even remotely decent at solving boards quickly, even with 0 perks, every boss brings 0 challenge or unique gameplay because the timer becomes so long and forgiving. The difficulty curve for later runs is non-existent. Getting to ~round 40, the mine density was no greater than a base Minesweeper Expert board, probably less. The music is uninspired and doesn't even loop properly. The game on default settings is a horrendous experience. Screen shake does not work on a game that requires precision and speed such as Minesweeper, turn this setting off immediately unless you want to miss click every board. This game has potential, but currently it squanders it in a pretty spectacular way. I can only imagine that for someone who is new at Minesweeper the experience is even worse. I don't think that this game is for anybody.

The store page says: "Think you know minesweeper? Think again" - this is wrong An in-game description says "This isn't Balatro" - this is correct It's just minesweeper. It's... Fine? But it's price tag is too steep for what's here, even with the discount There are loads of permanent upgrades, special tiles, playable cards, a trap system, and associated trap-disarming tools, but they're all more-or-less irrelevant and the game doesn't even wander out of it's way to explain how some of it's parts work. None of the game's selling points actually function to make the game better or even meaningfully different. You'll beat the game pretty easily just by playing basic minesweeper. Nothing the game limply throws at you will change this. There's a trap tile which makes it so that losing a single life will end your game, which just means "you now have the standard loss condition of minesweeper" The most interest the game generated was when I found that there were sets of "useless" items, so I spent an hour or so in the infinite mode trying to complete a set. The upgrade you get for doing so wasn't worth it, and the process of getting the set was so random that it seems vanishingly unlikely that you'll get it before completing a run. Play the demo instead - it's pretty much the full game but for a much more appealing price

这款扫雷+肉鸽游戏整体体验十分平庸。 最大的问题在于，基础的扫雷难度过低，熟练玩家白板零构筑就能通关95%的关卡，直接让肉鸽构筑体系变得毫无意义、形同虚设，所有流派搭配、卡牌选择都失去了价值。 剩余5%卡关内容，也并非设计合理的高难度关卡，只是无尽模式下必然会遇到的、无法靠推理破解的死猜局，倒逼玩家只能围绕探雷、回血构筑，大半卡牌与流派直接沦为鸡肋。比如部分暴露类卡牌，居然会高概率锁定已标记的地雷，在死猜局里几乎无效，设计逻辑十分不合理。 至于技能描述模糊等小问题，在核心玩法失衡的硬伤面前，根本不值一提，整体游玩体验大打折扣。

太神了，扫雷+肉鸽我还以为是多么有创意的玩法，一玩还是得二选一，选不对就掉血，死了就重开。 提供的构筑大半全是卵用没有的，一堆高稀有构筑还不如低稀有的能揭开雷的有用。 最神的是每打几关还得给你上个陷阱，什么叫揭开陷阱后随机给你乱插旗拔旗？ 什么脑回路能想到做出这种神人陷阱？插的旗还得去看有没有错，已经插的甚至还给你拔了，巨变态，玩到气笑了。 退款了，这游戏扫雷不扫雷，肉鸽不肉鸽的，想不明白核心受众到底在哪了

[h1]省流：棋盘非无猜，构筑搞自肃[/h1] 一开始是被肉鸽和美术吸引来的。美术风格也确实很好，震动太强了也可以设置里调小，视觉上确实很喜欢。肉鸽方面只能说很平庸。不知道为什么在能力获取方面做这么克制或者说恶意的设计，不管是永久强化（遗物）、方块还是卡牌都有数量上限。卡牌和方块我还能理解，但是永久强化的数量限制我只觉得是为了不让玩家爽，而陷阱的设计又进一步放大了这个点。很多陷阱是可以直接将你目前的构筑变得完全没用的，而且还不止一个。虽然看起来每次陷阱都是让你3选1的，但其实经常出现其中两个是同一个陷阱的情况，我甚至遇到过一两次3个陷阱都是同一个陷阱的情况，这不来搞笑的吗？游戏里确实有可以从收藏里删除陷阱的卡牌，但我玩了21小时才见到第一次，到现在30多小时没见到第二次。游戏里也有些奇怪（？）的设计，比如5个无效果的强化可以合并成一个顶级但实际上作用不大的强化，卡牌也有一个类似的设计，但在我看来还是没法盖过缺点。 但是最大的问题还是：这游戏生成的棋盘不是无猜的。这使得很多时候，特别是每把刚开始的前几关，很容易出现大量需要纯猜2选1的情况，无法通过推理来确定。你想要通关（打过16关解锁新内容），就必须要看运气。这不是说买两张卡牌就能解决的问题，前期金币少，而且能不能出帮你猜的卡牌也是看运气的。就这一个核心原因，导致在我看来就算有前面那些缺点但也能80分的游戏，直接不及格。太破坏游戏体验了，从好评变为差评。 希望作者研究下怎么生成无猜棋盘，这真的能让游戏加分很多，让人更愿意玩：[url=https://sources.debian.org/src/sgt-puzzles/20170606.272beef-1/mines.c]Simon Tatham的无猜扫雷[/url]

[b] TL;DR [/b] If you like classic Minesweeper, there is a very good chance you'll enjoy this. Otherwise, probably avoid. The game plays essentially like Minesweeper, but adds roguelike deckbuilding elements such as permanent effects (similar to relics), consumable cards (similar to potions), and additional tiles that effectively represent your deck. You clear Minesweeper boards that increase in size each stage, and after every stage you receive coins and visit a shop where you can buy the aforementioned items. The background music is relaxing, and opening tiles feels satisfying, especially when you get combos going. The screen-shake effect gave me a headache, but thankfully it can be disabled in the settings. Overall, I quite like the presentation and have very few complaints there. Every 4th stage is a "boss fight", where you get a timer based on your score. However, from my experience the timer is so generous (like 45 min for a large board) that it barely matters in practice and might as well be removed entirely. After each boss fight, you also have to add a trap tile to your deck. These are negative effects that you have to deal with, such as removing information from tiles. Some items can provide trap fixers, which let you remove these trap tiles after revealing them. In principle, you only need to clear 16 stages to receive a victory message, but the game can continue indefinitely. As other reviewers have noted, this is not particularly difficult if you are already familiar with Minesweeper. To me, the actual objective feels more like achieving the highest possible score, which you get from clearing tiles and certain special items. This creates an interesting tradeoff between buying information-gathering items (to deal with the frequent 50/50 situations common in Minesweeper), handling traps, and maximizing points. Especially once your deck is filled with multiple traps and you are only allowed a small number of mistakes, progressing becomes increasingly difficult. Personally, I do not enjoy endless mode in roguelikes very much, because by that point your build is usually finished and there is little left to do, but mileage may vary. [b] Suggestions [/b] [list] [*] I do not like that a run only gets added to the highscore after you lose. [*] The highscore list should also track highest stage reached, not just points. [*] Unlocks currently only happen after beating stage 16. I think unlocks tied to stages or boss clears instead would make endless mode feel more rewarding. [*] Boss stages feel almost identical to normal stages. Instead of using a timer, it would be more interesting to have different boss encounters with unique effects, similar to how certain traps work. [*] Many items feel completely useless or even harmful. Some items literally say "does nothing". For example, one tile automatically flags a nearby enemy but does not reveal how many enemies surround it. In many situations, this actually removes information, making the board harder to solve. [*] Tile upgrades are currently tied to rare and epic cards, which makes them difficult to obtain and unreliable. I assume the idea is to give players something to keep pursuing in endless mode, but I think there should be an additional upgrade method, such as spending coins after reaching a certain number of stages. [/list] Overall, I think this is a very solid twist on Minesweeper with a good presentation and some genuinely interesting ideas, even if parts of the roguelike system still feel underdeveloped. I hope the developers continue supporting and improving the game instead of abandoning it. The game also runs perfectly fine on the Steam Deck using the trackpad as mouse.

Two months of not a single update, they finally do one and it doesn't make the game any better. I played the update for less than an hour and two things stood out as broken to me. First: They added the ability to spend coins on upgrading your tiles, it doesn't work properly. You upgrade a tile but it doesn't show you the new effect (which is raising how many of said tile can spawn on the board) so I'm not sure if it works at all. Second: The boss challenges, I got one that randomly locks blank tiles so you can't click on it. When you're down to a handful, for example four blanks and one enemy to flag to win, they all just lock over and over again. That's just what I found in a few runs, who knows what else is broken or untested.

Infinity Sweeper mixes classic logic with roguelike runs, letting you buy cards that twist the rules and reshape each grid. Tense and endlessly replayable as every upgrade shifts your strategy.
